rows.title: File:Budapest protest 2018-12-16 20-03-39.jpg
rows.artist: Vauia Rex
rows.description:
Budapest protest against the overtime work act 2018-12-16, march from Kossuth squere to the MTVA building at Pacsirtamező utca. At the intersection with Perc utca and Dévai Bíró Mátyás tér. Facing north.

The flag of the European Union and the flag of Momentum Movement are visible.

The sign on the right reads: "Bojkott! Új rendszerváltozást!" meaning "Boycott! New regime change!"

Note that "Rendszerváltozás" is the Hungarian term specifically refering to the end of communism in 1989-90, but literally just means "system change" or "regime change".

rows.title: File:Budapest protest 2018-12-16 20-05-13.jpg
rows.artist: Vauia Rex
rows.description:
Budapest protest against the overtime work act 2018-12-16, march from Kossuth squere to the MTVA building at Pacsirtamező utca. At the intersection with Perc utca and Dévai Bíró Mátyás tér. Facing east, towards Perc utca.

Multiple protesters carrying a Hungarian flag.

The yellow sign reads: "KERESZTÉNY VAGYOK ÉS NEM FIDESZES! EZT ADD ÖSSZE, ZSOLT!" meaning "I am christian and not a Fidesz voter! Take that, Zsolt"

"Zsolt" refers to Zsolt Semjén, leader of Christian Democratic People's Party (KDNP), Fidesz's junior coalition patner.

rows.title: File:Táncsics Straße 26, Grabsteine, 2022 Budapest.jpg
rows.description: One storey, listed, Baroque residential building. Museum and Medieval Jewish Prayer House on its groundfloor. In the two extreme right axes of the ground floor, the supposed 15th century façade of the house is presented (mural, a forward floor resting on consoles). - The cemetery of the Jewish community that in the 13th century settled in Buda located at the southwestern foot of Buda Castle hill. The Fehérvári castle gate area (and the Szent György Square) was the Jewish quarter till 15th century. Just next to the gate stand the Old (13th century) Synagogue. The gate called as Jewish gate too. - The Ottoman era Jewish cemetery located close to the northeast castle walls, in the nearby of the 15th century ('New') synagogue (now remains can be see in the garden at #21-23 Táncsics Street) in the late medieval Jewis Quarter. In the gateway at #26 Táncsics Street a couple Jewish gravestones from these cemeteries exhibited. - The facade monument plaque (install. 1967) inscription is: ~"In the 15th century, it was the house of the Buda Castle Jewish prefect. In the 16-17th centuries, it was a prayer house for Syrian Jews. The present building was built in the eighteenth century from the remains of two medieval houses. Restored in 1966" Description based Budapest100 research /researchers: Barbara Szij, Ágoston Takács /: "built to a civic house in the 14th century. Rebuilt/remodelled several times. Based on 17th century murals it was the house Buda Castle rabbi or it was synagogue. After the restoration in 1964!, it was transformed into an exhibition space showcasing medieval Jews in Buda. Since 2018, it has also been operating as a synagogue of EMIH - Hungarian Jewish Association on weekends" - In groundfoor room are two red painted symbols with Hebrew inscription (found in 1964): 'David Star - Priestlys blessing' (4 Moses 6:24-26) AND 'Bow - Prayer of Hannah' (1 Samuel 2:4) - This building was a participiant of the 'Budapest 100 2022' event. Part of the event was a presentation by Ágoston Takács, archaeologist, museologist and head of the medieval lapidary of the Budapest History Museum (BTM) The presentation title: 'On the history of the synagogue and the medieval Jews of Buda' - Part of the Budapest World Heritage protected architectural ensembles - 26 Táncsics Street, Várnegyed neighborhood, District I of Budapest.

rows.title: File:Aram Bajakian at The Glass House Project.jpg
rows.description:
Musician Aram Bajakian playing as part of the Glass House Project, at Budapest Music Center.

The Glass House Project began as a tribute to the 70th Anniversary of the Holocaust in Hungary. The intention was to look at the largest picture of pre-war Hungarian music and to represent the breadth and scope of Hungarian musics from many traditions, with a focus on the incredibly rich and diverse Hungarian Jewish musical landscape.

Members:

Frank London (trumpet) Pablo Aslan (bass), Aram Bajakian (guitar) Jake Shulman-Ment (violin) Yoni Halevy (drums) Edina Szirtes Mókus (violin, voice), Miklós Lukács (cimbalom/tsimbl), Béla Ágoston (winds)
